references.text: Moses sprinkles the blood of the covenant and says, 'See, this is the blood of the covenant' ([ref:2 Mos 24:8|Exodus 24:8]). Jesus' words about the cup as 'the new covenant in my blood' are a direct parallel to the ratification of the covenant at Sinai, where the blood sealed the covenant between God and the people.

Jeremiah prophesies about a new covenant that the Lord will make with the house of Israel ([ref:Jer 31:31-34|Jeremiah 31:31-34]). Jesus declares that the cup is 'the new covenant in my blood,' thus fulfilling this prophecy concerning the new covenant.
Zechariah speaks of covenant blood that releases prisoners ([ref:Sak 9:11|Zechariah 9:11]). The connection between covenant blood and liberation points forward to Jesus' covenant sacrifice.

Matthew's parallel account of the Last Supper, where Jesus takes the cup and says, 'This is my blood, the blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins' ([ref:Matt 26:27-28|Matthew 26:27-28]).

Mark's parallel account of the Last Supper, where Jesus gives the cup to the disciples and says, 'This is my blood, the blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many' ([ref:Mark 14:23-24|Mark 14:23-24]).

Paul quotes Jesus' words about the cup: 'This cup is the new covenant in my blood' ([ref:1 Kor 11:25|1 Corinthians 11:25]). This is the earliest written record of the institution of the Lord's Supper and closely corresponds to Luke's version.

Paul speaks of the cup of blessing as 'a sharing in the blood of Christ' ([ref:1 Kor 10:16|1 Corinthians 10:16]). The cup in the Lord's Supper grants participation in the new covenant through Christ's blood.

The book of Hebrews quotes Jeremiah 31 about the new covenant and explains that the first covenant has become obsolete ([ref:Hebr 8:8-13|Hebrews 8:8-13]). Jesus institutes this new covenant with his own blood.
Jesus is the mediator of a new covenant, and in the old covenant, blood was used to dedicate the covenant ([ref:Hebr 9:15-20|Hebrews 9:15-20]). Jesus' blood sealed the new covenant in a similar way.

Jesus' blood, which is 'the mediator of the new covenant,' speaks more strongly than the blood of Abel ([ref:Hebr 12:24|Hebrews 12:24]). The power of covenant blood is emphasized as central to the new covenant.

God raised Jesus, 'the great shepherd of the sheep,' from the dead 'by the blood of the eternal covenant' ([ref:Hebr 13:20|Hebrews 13:20]). Here, Jesus' blood as the foundation of the covenant is confirmed.
